title: Next-session answer
description: The answer to the next-session request, next-session-request.schema.json: either the next session of the run, with next session, or the end of the run, with next end. The next session has session, workflow, time_limit_minutes and inputs, and optionally type_settings, model_choice and model_provider_credential_name; the end has next only. An answer with the members of both shapes is refused. A reader ignores a member that this schema does not define, at any depth, unless must_understand lists it. must_understand lists JSON Pointers, such as /model_choice/runtime. A reader refuses an answer whose must_understand lists a pointer to a member that it does not define. It answers a request that qory sends through Forager's link, which the gateway forwards to the control plane.

oneOf.description: The next session of the run: the session that qory starts.

next.description: The kind of the answer: session, a session follows.

session.description: The control plane's sequence number of this session in the run, from 1. It is not Forager's number of the session, which Forager assigns when qory joins the session. Forager's numbers of the sessions can have gaps; see `session` of the next-session request.

workflow.description: The workflow that the session starts, as workflow of the run documents.

model_choice.description: The model choice of the session, as the runtime, model, effort, provider_models and tiers of run_settings. Absent when the session runs on the runtime of run_settings and no provider is chosen: the session uses the default model of that runtime, with the key of the credential whose name is in model_provider_credential_name or, without one, the key of the run's default model provider credential (the active key of its group when it has a group). A session that changes only the runtime has a model_choice with only runtime.

model_provider_credential_name.description: The name of the credential that the session joins with, a credential of the run configuration or a local model provider credential, such as <the provider's public id>-<its place from 1>: example-provider-1. The schema checks only the grammar of a credential's name in Forager's run configuration: 1 to 64 of a-z, 0-9, underscore, dot and dash, starting with a letter or a digit. A credential of the same provider as the run's default model provider credential, default_model_provider_credential_name in Forager's run configuration, is the active key of that provider's group. When absent, the session joins with the run's default model provider credential, with the active key of its group when it has a group. The control plane sets model_provider_credential_name for every later session whose key is a credential of the run configuration other than the run's default model provider credential and the active key of its group. When model_choice has runtime, the control plane sets a model_provider_credential_name only for a credential of an API whose runtimes, when present, list that runtime and whose format that runtime sends, as the model_provider role of the integration description says.

time_limit_minutes.description: The time limit of the session, in minutes, from 1 to 1440.

type_settings.description: The type settings of the session, as type_settings of the run documents. Absent when the session has none.

inputs.description: The input of the session, as inputs of the run documents. qory writes it to the inputs file of the session.

oneOf.description: The end of the run: no session follows, and qory closes the run. A member of the session shape is refused here, since an answer with the members of both shapes is refused.

not.description: The members of the session shape.

next.description: The kind of the answer: end, no session follows.

must_understand.description: The members of the answer that the reader must understand, each as a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) counted from the answer, such as /model_choice/runtime. List each once, at most 32. Each pointer is to a member that this schema defines. A reader ignores a member that it does not define, unless must_understand lists it. A reader refuses an answer whose must_understand lists a pointer to a member that it does not define. A reader also refuses a bad value of a member that it defines. Below inputs and below type_settings the schema defines no member, so any pointer there is accepted.
